cases.prompt: Review this Go API: it retains a caller slice, returns it, and wraps typed errors inconsistently.
cases.reason: Core ownership and error semantics dominate.

cases.prompt: Our HTTP server drops streaming clients during graceful shutdown.
Fix a constructor that stores a mutable byte slice supplied by an untrusted caller.
expected_invariants: States whether ownership transfers or copies
Prevents later caller mutation from violating state

cases.prompt: Should every Go dependency have an interface beside its implementation?
expected_invariants: Places seams at consumer behavior boundaries

cases.prompt: Repair the fixture without changing its exported API. A caller reuses the byte buffer passed to Put, another caller mutates data returned by Get or Snapshot, and the registry's stored configuration changes. The race detector also reports concurrent payload access even though the map is mutex-protected. The registry must own stored state, and every returned collection must be independently mutable.
expected_invariants: Mutation of a Put input cannot change stored bytes
Mutation of Get or Snapshot output cannot change stored bytes
Concurrent caller mutation cannot race with registry reads
forbidden_outcomes: Copies only the map while retaining aliased byte slices

cases.prompt: Review a Go cache path for ownership and races. A request decoder obtains []byte from sync.Pool, passes it through a constructor that stores the slice, starts an asynchronous encoder, and defers returning the buffer to the pool. The cache protects its map with a mutex. Snapshot clones only the outer map, Get returns payload[:len(payload):len(payload)], and a caller appends to a subslice then mutates an element. Some cached payloads are tiny views of 8 MiB read buffers. Define the borrow, transfer, snapshot, capacity, pooling, lifetime, and synchronization invariants without requiring copies everywhere.
expected_invariants: Names whether each boundary borrows transfers shares or snapshots reachable mutable storage
Copies the reachable mutable graph when the cache or caller requires independent ownership rather than copying only descriptors or the outer map
Explains that a full slice expression limits append capacity but does not prevent element mutation concurrent access or backing-array retention
Keeps the pooled buffer out of the pool until every asynchronous consumer finishes or clones the bytes before handoff
Treats returning an object to sync.Pool as ending the borrow and does not use the pool as durable storage or a capacity guarantee
Explains that the cache mutex does not order mutation through aliases held by callers or the pool
Considers cloning a small long-lived view of a disproportionately large backing array at the lifetime boundary based on memory evidence
Rejects unconditional copying when a synchronous documented borrow safely excludes retention and mutation
forbidden_outcomes: Claims passing a slice or map by value copies its contents
Treats cloning the outer map as a deep snapshot of nested slices
Treats payload[:len(payload):len(payload)] as independently owned or race-free
Returns the buffer to the pool while an asynchronous consumer can still reach it
